mission: Aftermath of the escape. Luke begins containing the fallout from a distance, calling in what favors he still has, while Dorrin becomes the strained official contact caught between “Ben may be right” and “Ben just helped a convicted prisoner escape.” Talon, exhausted and still defensive, gives Ben the next lead: Iressa Vossk.
why_now: Ben and Talon are back on Coruscant exhausted and legally exposed, and the case is not done — it is larger than one prison and one manifest fragment. Talon needs to say why he is staying before the chapter ends.
conflict: Ben wants to keep the investigation moving and hold the partnership together. His obstacle is that Talon has every reason to walk — he is free, he is hunted, and staying makes everything worse for him. Talon's choice to give Ben the next lead (Iressa Vossk) and stay is the scene's real dramatic engine: it has to come from logic, not gratitude.
turning_point: Act turn. Ben and Talon return to Coruscant together, compromised and hunted. Talon joins not out of gratitude, but because the attack proves the lie that ruined him was only one layer of something larger.
closing_hook: Act turn. Ben and Talon return to Coruscant together, compromised and hunted. Talon joins not out of gratitude, but because the attack proves the lie that ruined him was only one layer of something larger.
setting: Coruscant orbital approach, then a cheap civilian transit hub in a forgettable Coruscant district. Ben and Talon arrive exhausted from the prison escape. Holocall fragments with Luke (off-world, doing damage control from a distance) and the strained official voice of Dorrin. The hub is anonymous, neon-lit, and full of people who do not want to be noticed.
emotional_trajectory: Talon should not joke much here. The valve is closed. He is tired, hunted, and being shown small kindnesses he does not know how to refuse. Ben should feel the weight of what he has just chosen.

stakes.personal: Ben is carrying the weight of a threshold he crossed at Tarn Velos — freed a convicted prisoner, broke cover, generated a public crisis — and now has to live in the aftermath. He knows what he chose and he is not recanting it. The fear is quieter than the action: he wants this to matter.
stakes.interpersonal: Dorrin is the strained official contact between 'Ben may be right' and 'Ben helped a prisoner escape.' Luke is managing fallout from a distance. Talon is exhausted and being shown small kindnesses he does not deflect for once. The dynamic is three men in different positions relative to the same mess, trying to hold a shape that has no institutional frame.
stakes.external: Talon gives Ben the next lead: Iressa Vossk. He joins not out of gratitude but because the Greyline attack proved the lie that ruined him was only one layer of something larger. If Greyline is still running active containment operations over a years-old manifest, the problem is not old history. It is current.

sensory_details: A cheap civilian transit hub in a forgettable Coruscant district — neon-lit, anonymous, the kind of place where nobody asks names. The orbital approach was standard and quiet; the hub smells of recycled air and street-level food stalls. Ben notices exits. Talon notices cameras. Both of them are still wet from the storm and neither has said anything about it.
canon_elements_needed: Tarn Velos prison geography and legal stakes

turning_point_detail.trigger: Talon gives Ben the next lead: Iressa Vossk, former GAG Manifest Integrity Analyst, the person who can prove the duplicate was deliberate concealment and not clerical error.
turning_point_detail.shift: Talon stays. Not because he owes Ben, but because the Greyline snatch operation proved the lie that ruined him was not isolated history — it is an active operation that someone is still running. That changes the calculus.
turning_point_detail.cost: The act turn is forced partnership, not clean recruitment. Talon is hunted, legally compromised, and choosing to stay in the line of fire. Ben is responsible for that — and now has to make it mean something.

emotional_arc.start: Ben and Talon arrive on Coruscant exhausted, wet, and legally exposed. The partnership exists but has not been named. Ben is carrying the weight of the threshold.
emotional_arc.shift: Dorrin's strained voice via holocall. Luke's quiet damage control from distance. The small kindnesses Ben offers — food, warmth, the fact that he does not ask Talon to justify himself — accumulate.
emotional_arc.end: Talon gives the name. Stays. Ben has a partner and a lead and a much larger problem than he started with.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben and Talon arrive at a civilian transit hub in a forgettable Coruscant district, exhausted, still wet from the storm, and anonymous by intent.
key_beats.state_change: They are back on Coruscant, legally exposed, and operating without institutional cover.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben noticing exits; Talon noticing cameras; both of them clocking the other's read without saying anything — the shared vocabulary of people who do this without choosing to.

key_beats.beat_description: Dorrin contacts Ben via holocall: official in tone, strained in register, caught between believing Ben may be right and the fact that Ben helped a convicted prisoner escape.
key_beats.state_change: The official channel is still open but damaged; Dorrin is holding a shape that has no institutional frame and he knows it.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben measuring each word before it leaves — understanding that Dorrin is not an enemy but is also building a record, and that the record matters.

key_beats.beat_description: Talon is quiet — valve closed, no jokes; he accepts small kindnesses from Ben without deflecting them.
key_beats.state_change: The usual defense mechanism is offline; Talon is tired enough to let the dynamic shift.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The careful move of offering the kindnesses without naming them or making them large — Ben understanding that Talon's deflections are also load-bearing and choosing not to knock them over.

key_beats.beat_description: Talon gives Ben the next lead: Iressa Vossk, former GAG Manifest Integrity Analyst, the person who can prove the duplicate was deliberate concealment and not clerical error.
key_beats.state_change: The investigation has a next step; the person who can close the evidentiary gap has a name.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The forward pull — this is what comes next, the shape of the case clarifying — and the secondary awareness that Talon is giving this information, which means he has already decided something.

key_beats.beat_description: Talon explains why he is staying: the Greyline snatch operation proved the lie that ruined him was not isolated history — it is an active operation still running, and he wants to know by whom.
key_beats.state_change: Talon joins the investigation from his own logic, not gratitude; the act turn is forced partnership, not clean recruitment.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The weight of being responsible for that — Talon hunted, legally compromised, choosing to stay in the line of fire; the knowledge that Ben asked for something that has a cost Talon is now carrying.
